title: These are the AI world's biggest questions as the White House hashes out a framework with OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic
excerpt: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google met in D.C. to review Trump's AI oversight framework amid cybersecurity concerns and regulatory questions.
content_html:
By Stephen Council

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

The AI world is looking to D.C. for clarity.

On Tuesday, staffers from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and other tech companies convened in Washington to review the administration's new framework for reviewing advanced AI models. Now, the rest of the industry eagerly awaits answers on what will be included in the framework — a structured way for President Donald Trump's administration to evaluate AI models' cyber capabilities.

The framework represents a turning point for AI oversight. While Trump's administration has adopted a light-touch regulatory approach, rapid advances in AI models for cybersecurity and hacking are beginning to upend it.

It's an open question how the new process will shape up and affect the release and adoption of new AI models. The New York Times reported on Tuesday that White House officials said at the meeting that the federal government plans to review only certain types of AI models from companies like Anthropic and OpenAI for potential security risks and does not plan to review open-source AI models so far, though these plans could change as the technology advances. Open-source models allow anyone to download or modify the code for free.

An executive order in early June directed officials to develop a "benchmarking process to assess the advanced cyber capabilities of AI models" within 60 days. The deadline has passed.

Here are the major outstanding questions.

How committed is the Trump administration to its stance on AI?

The administration's AI oversight approach has been defined by its light-touch regulatory stance. Its AI Action Plan, released in 2025, said that regulation might end up "paralyzing" the industry, and called on agencies to "dismantle unnecessary regulatory barriers that hinder the private sector."

The executive order in June acknowledged a new reality in which AI models from Anthropic and OpenAI have shown marked improvements in coding, finding cybersecurity exploits, and working on longer-term tasks.

The framework, as sketched in the June order, will require companies to share their AI models with the government for up to 30 days before releasing them to the public, giving the government a head start in assessing their cyber capabilities.

Crucially, Trump's executive order described the framework as "voluntary," though it's an open question how the administration would treat companies that skip the process. Jessica Ji, an analyst at Georgetown's Center for Security and Emerging Technology, said it seems like officials are trying to create a "soft compliance regime."

"Ideally, they can say we're not regulating, this is a voluntary program, but all of the companies whose models they think present potential national security risks would comply," she said.

Which AI models will the framework cover?

Regulating AI is tricky. Rules could target the top-tier labs, specific products, or individual AI models. If regulators home in on the models, more questions pop up. Do they base their rules on the models' size, or when they're released, or what they're capable of?

The conversation in D.C. over recent months has turned around the AI models' capabilities because of new developments like Anthropic's Mythos model and OpenAI's security incident with the AI company Hugging Face.

Trump's executive order asked his agencies to develop a definition of the "covered frontier models" that would be vetted by his administration. Chinese open-source and open-weight models, which have sparked furor in the industry recently because of their advanced capabilities, are almost certainly part of the Tuesday conversation, Ji said.

She added that figuring out ways to categorize AI models is a crucial step for the rulemakers.

What authority will the government have over the leading AI juggernauts?

It's unclear so far how the framework will affect the rollout of AI models, especially if it truly feels voluntary to companies. Ji said she's curious whether there will be any clear guidance on what the administration can do if it finds a dangerous capability while testing unreleased technology.

In June, Trump's Commerce Department responded to cybersecurity concerns about an Anthropic model by issuing an export control that barred the company from granting foreign nationals access. Anthropic ended up pulling down all access to the model until it reached a deal with the administration.

Ji said it's unlikely the administration would keep resorting to export controls, though it's unclear what other levers they might pull to intervene in a model release or to pressure a company to change its product.

She said the meeting will provide more clarity on who in the Trump administration makes the decisions around AI oversight and cybersecurity.

"We're trying to figure out who are the new kind of power players, who has influence in the administration on this set of issues, right now," Ji said.

Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI did not immediately respond to requests for comment from Business Insider.

content_html_zh:
作者：Stephen Council 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

人工智能世界正在关注华盛顿特区。 为了清楚起见。

周二，来自 OpenAI、Anthropic、谷歌和其他科技公司的员工聚集在华盛顿，审查政府审查先进人工智能模型的新框架。 现在，该行业的其他成员热切地等待该框架中将包含哪些内容的答案——这是唐纳德·特朗普总统政府评估人工智能模型网络能力的结构化方式。

该框架代表了人工智能监管的一个转折点。 尽管特朗普政府采取了宽松的监管方法，但网络安全和黑客攻击的人工智能模型的快速进步正开始颠覆它。

新流程将如何形成并影响新人工智能模型的发布和采用，这是一个悬而未决的问题。 《纽约时报》周二报道称，白宫官员在会议上表示，联邦政府计划仅审查 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 等公司的某些类型的人工智能模型是否存在潜在的安全风险，目前不打算审查开源人工智能模型，不过这些计划可能会随着技术的进步而改变。 开源模型允许任何人免费下载或修改代码。

6 月初的一项行政命令指示官员在 60 天内制定“评估人工智能模型先进网络能力的基准流程”。 截止日期已过。

以下是主要的未决问题。

特朗普政府对人工智能的立场有多坚定？

政府的人工智能监管方法是由其宽松的监管立场决定的。 其于 2025 年发布的人工智能行动计划表示，监管可能最终导致该行业“瘫痪”，并呼吁各机构“消除阻碍私营部门的不必要的监管障碍”。

6 月份的行政命令承认了一个新的现实，即来自 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 的人工智能模型在编码、发现网络安全漏洞和处理长期任务方面显示出显着的改进。

正如 6 月份的命令中所概述的，该框架将要求公司在向公众发布人工智能模型之前与政府共享其人工智能模型长达 30 天，从而使政府在评估其网络能力方面占据先机。

至关重要的是，特朗普的行政命令将该框架描述为“自愿”，尽管政府将如何对待跳过该流程的公司仍是一个悬而未决的问题。 乔治城安全与新兴技术中心分析师杰西卡·吉表示，官员们似乎正在试图建立一个“软合规制度”。

“理想情况下，他们可以说我们没有进行监管，这是一个自愿计划，但他们认为其模式存在潜在国家安全风险的所有公司都会遵守，”她说。

该框架将涵盖哪些人工智能模型？

监管人工智能是很棘手的。 规则可以针对顶级实验室、特定产品或单个人工智能模型。 如果监管机构关注这些模型，就会出现更多问题。 他们的规则是否基于模型的尺寸、发布时间或模型的能力？

在华盛顿的谈话 近几个月来，由于 Anthropic 的 Mythos 模型等新发展以及 OpenAI 与人工智能公司 Hugging Face 发生的安全事件，人工智能模型的能力发生了转变。

特朗普的行政命令要求他的机构制定“涵盖的边境模式”的定义，并由他的政府审查。 吉说，中国的开源和开放权重模型最近因其先进的功能而在业界引起了轩然大波，几乎肯定会成为周二讨论的一部分。

她补充说，找出对人工智能模型进行分类的方法对于规则制定者来说是至关重要的一步。

政府对领先的人工智能巨头有什么权力？

到目前为止，尚不清楚该框架将如何影响人工智能模型的推出，特别是如果它确实对公司来说是自愿的。 吉说，她很好奇是否会有任何明确的指导，说明政府在测试未发布的技术时发现危险能力时可以做什么。

6 月，特朗普商务部通过发布出口管制措施，禁止该公司向外国人授予访问权限，以回应对人择模型的网络安全担忧。 Anthropic 最终取消了对该模型的所有访问权限，直到与政府达成协议。

吉表示，政府不太可能继续诉诸出口管制，但目前尚不清楚他们可能会采取哪些其他手段来干预模型发布或迫使公司改变产品。

她表示，这次会议将更清楚地表明特朗普政府中谁在人工智能监督和网络安全方面做出决策。

吉说：“我们现在正在努力找出谁是新型权力参与者，谁对政府在这一系列问题上有影响力。”

Anthropic、谷歌和 OpenAI 没有立即回应《商业内幕》的置评请求。
